analyst_view.overall: Hajduk Split (13th, 6 pts) host Sint-Truiden (10th, 7 pts) with both still in range of the knockout places, so neither side has a reason to hold back. Poljud is closed to regular fans after a UEFA punishment; about 8,000 invited children will be in the stands, with a couple of hundred Sint-Truiden fans on VIP tickets. Gonzalo Garcia said on Wednesday that everyone except Brajkovic, Ivusic and Livaja (back problem) is fit, so Hadzikadunic and Pajaziti are back from injury and wingers Soticek and Sanyang return after being rested at the weekend. Garcia expects an aggressive, high-pressing Sint-Truiden that attacks space through Sego and Martin, and no absentees are reported for the visitors; both clubs play again on Sunday. Italian referee Matteo Marchetti is named, and the numbers already trim cards about 7% for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.4 Hajduk, 1.6 Sint-Truiden), with both sides' recent scoring already in the momentum adjustment and Livaja's absence on the list. The news since the last view is good for Hajduk: centre-back Hadzikadunic and midfielder Pajaziti are fit again and Soticek and Sanyang are back, so Hajduk are close to full strength at both ends and nothing points clearly up or down. I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, split evenly, with Hajduk's recent corner count nudged up and Sint-Truiden's down by momentum. Soticek and Sanyang back on the wings helps Hajduk's wide play, while Sint-Truiden's pressing and runs in behind are more about quick attacks than crosses, so the two cancel out and I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already trimmed for referee Marchetti's low card record (-7%) and both sides' recent counts. I keep a small lean lower, to about 3.3: with Poljud closed to regular fans and only invited children and a few hundred away supporters in, there is far less crowd pressure on players and referee, which the numbers can't see. Sint-Truiden's high press could bring a few tactical fouls, which keeps the size small.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Sint-Truiden's busy attacking and Hajduk's tight recent defending are both in the momentum adjustment; Garcia expects an open game against a pressing side and plans to attack the space behind it, but Hajduk's returning players only bring them back to their usual strength, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already trimmed for Hajduk conceding few on target lately (Sint-Truiden -7%). Hadzikadunic's return strengthens Hajduk's defence but he was in the side that built that record, and Livaja's absence is counted, so nothing new changes how often either keeper is tested and I stay at 9.1.
